caption:
Microsoft unveiled Maia 300, its third-generation custom AI chip, on Monday.

It plans multi-gigawatt deployments starting next year, potentially more than one million chips, and claims about 40% more useful computing per megawatt than leading GPU systems.

Can in-house chips loosen Nvidia's grip on AI?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: Reuters · Photo: Microsoft

slides.headline: Microsoft unveils *Maia 300* AI chip, eyes over a million next year

slides.heading: Built on *2-nanometer* chiplets
paras: Maia 300 is Microsoft's third-generation AI chip. Its main compute chiplet uses TSMC's 2-nanometer process, while other chiplets use 3-nanometer technology.
Each chip carries 288 GB of HBM4 memory with 18 TB/s of bandwidth, according to Microsoft's specs.

slides.heading: Aimed at *Nvidia's* grip
paras: A Maia 300 rack holds 96 chips and draws about 167 kilowatts. Nvidia's GB300 rack, with 72 GPUs, uses about 142 kilowatts.
Microsoft claims about 40% more useful computing per megawatt than leading GPU systems, but did not name the systems it compared.

paras.t: Deployments of multiple gigawatts start next year.

slides.hook: Big Tech is racing to build its own AI chips. Follow to see who pulls ahead.
